abstract_summary: Persistent memory is entering production-oriented agent platforms to help long-horizon agents accumulate experience across sessions. Yet a post-task curator agent restricted to completed trajectories can preserve errors, overgeneralize partial evidence, or retain stale knowledge. We introduce environment-probing cur...
citation: Grounding Agent Memory: Environment-Probing Curation for Enterprise Agents. Susheel Suresh, Hazel Mak, Sahil Bhatnagar, Chhaya Methani, Alejandro Gutierrez Munoz. 2026-09-10. https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11060

support_verification.reason: The results table includes confidence intervals and the metrics appendix defines exclusions from task-agent cost and tool calls, supporting the precision claim.

positive_signals: The paper introduces environment-probing curation, a deployment-compatible extension that gives an asynchronous curator agent least-privilege, read-only world tools to check, scope, and refresh candidate memories without retraining or changing the task agent, retriever, memory representation, or production write path.

The proposed environment-probing curation is novel relative to prior memory systems because existing post-task curation operates mainly over existing records, completed trajectories, grades, and usage signals, without live environment verification.
On the CLBench drift schedule, environment probing raises pass rate from 39 percent to 73 percent and total reward from 8.60 to 22.60 while reducing task-agent cost from 3.38 dollars to 1.68 dollars.

The reported improvements are attributable to write-time evidence quality rather than added task-agent capacity because the task-time model, tools, and read-only memory interface are held fixed across memory conditions.
The paper positions its contribution against factual and procedural memory systems and identifies the retrospective evidence boundary as the gap addressed by environment probing.

The paper provides sufficient implementation detail for reproducibility, including the GitHub Copilot SDK harness, per-task lifecycle, model names, embedding model, run counts, and full prompt specifications in appendices.

The paper acknowledges that probing does not improve over trajectory-only memory in all APEX worlds and that uncertainty intervals overlap, so subgroup effects are treated as mechanism interpretation rather than resolved findings.
The paper reports quantitative results with confidence intervals and clearly separates task-agent cost from distillation and curation cost, improving precision of the reported comparisons.
